title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that same candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic validator; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the registered evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising rapid draft generation of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. However, stochastic generation can produce mechanically verifiable defects (syntax, improper ordering, workflow violations) that create operational risk. Deterministic validators and constrained repair policies are therefore a common architectural defense [1], [2].

This work measures the marginal verifier-detected effect of inserting a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the exact same model output. By executing a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation per intent reused across both conditions) we isolate only the validator-and-repair effect on identical outputs rather than conflating generation variability across arms. Our confirmatory run uses 250 constrained synthetic intents, a declared model (gpt-5-mini), and a deterministic network validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) with deterministic, template-driven repair templates limited to syntactic and ordering fixes. We report concrete, artifact-backed counts and inferential results that quantify the upper bound on verifier-detected improvement for this pipeline and task scope.
sections.related_work:
Prior empirical and survey studies show LLMs can produce usable draft network configurations under controlled conditions but typically require external checks or human oversight to address remaining errors [1], [2], [3]. Deterministic verification and generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures are established as pragmatic mitigations for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains [4], [5], and Batfish-like formal analyses and header-space methods are mature validators for many forwarding and local-policy properties [6].

Work on automated repair in program-repair and configuration contexts demonstrates verifier-guided repair can correct many mechanically detectable errors but remains limited for deeper semantic or cross-device correctness without richer runtime tests [7]. Surveys and threat analyses further document that LLM-only self-correction is often unreliable without dependable external feedback and that prompt-injection is a practical concern for integrated pipelines [2], [5]. Our study differs by (i) adhering to shared_initial_candidate semantics so both conditions evaluate the identical generated candidate, (ii) reporting deterministic reconciliation and provider-call accounting (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair call), and (iii) archiving full validator and repair traces for auditable contingency accounting.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered with a confirmatory paired design (N_pairs = 250) and generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; analysis procedures (exact McNemar two‑sided, paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) and the single-repair policy were frozen in preregistration.

Execution semantics (shared_initial_candidate). For each intent exactly one initial LLM generation was executed and reused in both episodes: baseline (the candidate accepted as-is) and guarded (the candidate validated deterministically; if invalid, allow up to one automated repair and revalidate). This isolates the estimator to differences produced only by deterministic validation and the single permitted repair. Provider-call reconciliation records hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250 and repair = 1 (model_calls_used = 251).

Tasks, validator, and repair. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks; each task payload specified initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label. Tasks exercised workflow constraints (make-before-break switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns) and protected interfaces that must not be modified. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) which parses CLI sequences, computes parsed_command_count, checks required_sequence ordering, validates workflow constraints, and compares the final_state snapshot to the task's expected_final_state. Validator outputs include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag. Repair templates were deterministic and constrained to syntactic and ordering fixes (reordering commands to match required_sequence, splitting multi-command lines, correcting token-ordering errors). By design no multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis. Preregistered exclusion rules would remove vendor-parser failures or outputs containing credential-like tokens; in this confirmatory execution no episodes were excluded and contamination detectors flagged zero episodes (complete_pair_count = 250). The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to compute exact McNemar two‑sided p-values and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All artifacts (raw responses, per-episode validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis logs) are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The executor completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact records hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1.

Primary binary outcomes. Validator-scored successes were baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996) and guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency observed is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the lone exercised automated repair; the observed repair-conversion rate in the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%). Representative per-episode validator traces for passing episodes show parsed_command_count matching required_command_count and valid=true (examples archived; see task-000001, task-000002, task-000003 artifacts).

Statistical inference. The exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These outputs are recorded in the analysis results artifact.

Diagnostics and failure modes. Validator traces include validation_before/validation_after snapshots, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation lists. Across the confirmatory bank the dominant mechanical mismatch class was ordering/tokensequence errors that a constrained deterministic repair template can correct in a single pass. Other failure classes (vendor-specific semantic mismatches or cross-device emergent effects) were not observed within this synthetic partition. No episodes were excluded and contamination detectors reported zero flagged items.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting a near‑null marginal verifier effect. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases, and the guarded pipeline converted the sole failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the maximum verifier-detected improvement under the studied pipeline and scope.

Design and power considerations. The preregistration power calculation targeted detection of a 15 percentage-point absolute effect (assuming baseline ≈ 0.90) with N_pairs = 250 to achieve ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements and shifting the informative result toward a precision bound (the CI) rather than a hypothesis rejection. This highlights a common practical point: power planning is sensitive to baseline rates and constrained-task generators that bias toward well-formed outputs will tighten CIs but reduce observed effect sizes.

Operational implications and scope. These results do not imply validators are unnecessary. Instead they quantify marginal verifier-detected benefit in a narrow, synthetic task bank with a capable LLM and a validator that checks mechanically verifiable properties only. Deterministic validators remain essential where task scope, vendor heterogeneity, adversarial inputs, or higher operational stakes increase mechanically detectable error rates. Broader pipelines (multi-iteration repair, human escalation, live reachability tests, per-vendor fidelity) and exploratory partitions in the preregistration could materially change operational benefits but were not executed here.

Auditability and reproducibility. The execution and analysis artifacts archive detailed per-episode validator traces, repair traces, reconciliation manifests, provider-call accounting, and the immutable master-prompt reference. These artifacts support reproducibility of the reported contingency counts, provider-call accounting (shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1), and inferential outputs (bootstrap parameters and exact McNemar p-value). Researchers wishing to evaluate different repair policies or expanded partitions should follow the same shared_initial_candidate semantics when measuring the marginal effect of validators and repairs.

Limitations. The confirmatory run was intentionally constrained: (i) it used a synthetic/emulation partition only (community and production-like partitions were preregistered but not executed here), (ii) a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used, (iii) only one automated repair attempt was permitted, and (iv) the deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties but not live protocol dynamics or broader semantic correctness. These limitations restrict external validity and motivate preregistered follow-ups across partitions, models, and expanded repair policies.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. For 250 constrained synthetic intents generated by gpt-5-mini, baseline validator-passes were 249/250 and guarded passes 250/250; paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). The single discordant pair was fixed by the permitted deterministic repair. These results provide an empirical precision bound on verifier-detected improvement for the studied pipeline and task scope, but do not generalize to broader production heterogeneity, adversarial settings, or multi-iteration repair policies. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced throughout are archived in the registered evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature discovery, study selection, preregistration freeze, master-prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of manuscript technical content. A human Research Director performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and run accounting: declared model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Provider-call reconciliation records model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) with stage_counts recorded in the archived deterministic_reconciliation artifact.

Preregistration and immutable master prompt: the study was preregistered under the stated study identifier and the immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The evidence bundle contains the archived preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent cross-device interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
